INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 13 : Mirra Andreeva said she has learned to recover more quickly from setbacks after the Russian teenager completed an unbeaten run through the WTA Finals round-robin stage on Friday. Andreeva won her third group-stage match in straight sets after a late opponent change, having already secured a semi-final berth. The 19-year-old said the match against tournament alternate Diana Shnaider presented a new mental challenge because her progression was guaranteed, but she still wanted to preserve her momentum. "Before the tournament started I was afraid that I wouldn't win a match in the group," Andreeva told reporters. "Now you see how it turned out." The victory set up a first career meeting with American Jessica Pegula on Saturday. Andreeva described Pegula as one of the calmest players on tour and said coach Conchita Martinez would help prepare a detailed tactical plan.

Andreeva's poise in the desert marked a contrast with her emotional exit from Indian Wells in March, when she lost her title defence to Katerina Siniakova. Frustrated by the defeat, Andreeva launched into a profanity-laced tirade toward spectators and was booed as she left the court. The French Open champion said her response to losses has changed significantly over the course of the season. "Before it was super bad. I was very dramatic," Andreeva said. "It would take me a good two, three days. I wouldn't talk to anybody. I would just sit in the room locked up, not wanting to practice." Now, she said, disappointment generally lasts a day at most before the demands of the tour force her attention back to training or the next match. Andreeva said the Indian Wells setback came while she was trying to incorporate changes made in practice into her match play, which produced inconsistency and frustration. She said continued work on court, along with sessions with psychologists, helped her make progress. The results have followed. Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros this year and arrived at the WTA Finals for her singles debut after a 50-win season.

Source: Reuters

PARIS, Nov 14 : World champions South Africa's hopes of lifting the first Nations Championship trophy ended with their 21-19 defeat in France on Friday, coach Rassie Erasmus said. "I think we basically killed our dreams for the Nations Championship tonight with this performance and not getting the win and the four tries," Erasmus told a press conference. South Africa, who suffered their first defeat of the Nations Championship, remain top of the Southern Hemisphere table on 21 points, but New Zealand are one point behind with a game in hand. The Springboks will visit Ireland next week to conclude the group phase, while the All Blacks play Wales on Saturday before facing England the following Saturday.

Erasmus lamented his side's lack of discipline, as they conceded 11 penalties, eight of them in their own half. Lood de Jager was shown a yellow card for a high tackle, while Jasper Wiese was sent off for 20 minutes after the bunker upgraded his yellow card for a head-high hit. "It hurt us. That caused us in a big way. I don't think any of that was intentional, but I agree that it should have been cards," Erasmus said. "I guess the frustration is that the discipline cost us." France also received three yellow cards through scrumhalf Maxime Lucu, winger Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and tighthead prop Regis Montagne. Erasmus was far from satisfied with the performance. It was also South Africa's first defeat against Les Bleus at the Stade de France since 2005. "We didn't play well, so don’t find a lot of excuses," Erasmus said. "I don't think there's much more to blame than ourselves."

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 13 : Elina Svitolina overwhelmed Aryna Sabalenka in the deciding set to seal a 6-3 3-6 6-1 upset on Friday to reach the semi-finals of the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells, where she will face Linda Noskova. Svitolina absorbed and redirected Sabalenka's power effectively, breaking the Belarusian six times before sealing her first victory over her opponent in more than six years with a forehand winner on her fourth match point. With the win, Svitolina improved to 2-6 against Sabalenka in their career meetings.  "It was a bit of a roller-coaster match," Svitolina told reporters. "I played well in the first set but lost a little bit of rhythm. She played well in the second and served much better. I was really happy with the way I could come back in the third after losing the first game."

NO HANDSHAKE The Ukrainian again did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian and Belarusian players following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Svitolina, the 2018 WTA Finals champion, will face Noskova on Saturday for a place in the final. The defeat ended Sabalenka's season on a disappointing note. The second seed won Brisbane International in January and then Indian Wells and the Miami Open in March to complete the "Sunshine Double" but did not claim another title after that. Sabalenka also surrendered the world number one ranking to Elena Rybakina at the US Open. She had entered the season finale among the favourites after Rybakina withdrew on the eve of the tournament because of illness. Sabalenka declined to speak to the media following Friday's loss. ANDREEVA ROLLS Earlier in the day, tournament debutant Andreeva continued her impressive run with a 6-2 6-1 win over fellow Russian Diana Shnaider, her third straight-sets victory of the week. Shnaider, Andreeva's friend and doubles partner, replaced Karolina Muchova, who withdrew before the final day of round-robin matches with a gastrointestinal illness. Andreeva had already secured her place in the semi-finals before facing Shnaider and will meet American Jessica Pegula on Saturday. The eight-day, $10 million tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. The event will be played in Charlotte starting next year.

Source: Reuters

Nov 13 : The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has filed a challenge with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) over its ruling to reinstate Russian teams in next year's world championships, according to media reports on Friday.  The Athletic and TSN reported that the governing body's challenge is based on the non-disclosure of ties to Russia by two of the three CAS panel members involved in the decision. The IIHF and CAS did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.   The Lausanne-based court last month ordered the IIHF to admit Russian teams to five upcoming tournaments, beginning with the World Junior Championship in Alberta that runs from December 26 to January 5.

NEW YORK, Nov 13 : An internet trade group sued New York on Friday, seeking to block a state law requiring social media platforms that contain potentially addictive features to provide state-approved warning labels for users. In a complaint filed in federal court, NetChoice said the law violates the free speech protections of the US Constitution's First Amendment by compelling its members to convey the state's "preferred message" about online safety. The office of New York Attorney General Letitia James, who enforces the state's laws, declined immediate comment. NetChoice has more than 30 members including Alphabet's Google and YouTube, Facebook and Instagram parent Meta Platforms, Snapchat parent Snap and ByteDance's TikTok. It has filed many lawsuits challenging regulation of social media businesses.

Signed by Governor Kathy Hochul last December, the New York law requires social media platforms with infinite scrolling, auto-play and algorithmic feeds to warn about potential harm to younger users. It requires the display of a "warning" from the US Surgeon General that while social media may benefit some young users, "excessive use may be associated with significant mental health harms." The statement is modeled after findings in 2023 by former US Surgeon General Vivek Murthy. NetChoice said New York's law is "designed to block, burden, and browbeat social media users" by subjecting them to the warning when they sign on and after multiple hours of use, with no way to bypass it. "Unlike a static warning on a product label, these warnings repeatedly interrupt users and block access to protected speech," NetChoice said. NetChoice filed a similar lawsuit against California last month. It also said New York's law is similar to a Colorado law that a federal judge blocked in November 2025, citing the First Amendment. Colorado is appealing that decision. New York's law is scheduled to take effect on January 1.

Source: Reuters

CAPE TOWN, Nov 13 : Tunisia’s dismal run continued with a 2-0 home defeat by Libya in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Friday, while Mohamed Salah became Egypt’s record scorer in their 5-0 rout of Malawi. There were key wins for Cape Verde and Nigeria, who had made disappointing starts to the 2027 qualifying campaign, but there were also frustrating home draws for past winners South Africa and Zambia. Salah scored twice late on to take his international tally to 70 and surpass former captain Hossam Hassan’s record. New coach Ali Maher began his tenure with a comprehensive victory in Cairo that put Egypt top of Group B. Tunisia were the only one of Africa’s 10 teams at this year's World Cup to exit following the group stage, and they fired coach Sabri Lamouchi after their opening defeat.

Their woes continued against neighbours Libya on Friday as they lost 2-0 in Sfax to a penalty from Ali Youssef on the stroke of halftime and a 62nd minute effort from Hamdou El Houni.   The defeat left Tunisia with two points at the halfway stage of their Group H campaign and in danger of missing next year’s finals, which would end their record run of 17 successive appearances. Coach Mouin Chaabani’s short reign is also under threat. Cape Verde, who thrilled the neutrals with their run to the second round at the World Cup, had lost their opening qualifiers in September but were back to winning ways on Friday with a 4-2 home triumph over Liberia, with debutant Derensili Sanches Fernandes from Huddersfield Town among the scorers. Nigeria made multiple changes to their line-up after a 3-0 loss to Guinea Bissau in their last outing two months ago and bounced back with giant striker Tolu Arokodare scoring twice in their 3-1 win over Tanzania. CAME FROM BEHIND Defender Jean Girumugisha scored seven minutes from time for tiny Burundi to draw 1-1 away at Zambia in Group I while Ryan Ogam’s 90th minute strike saw Kenya hold South Africa 2-2 in Johannesburg in Group D. Mali came from behind to beat Rwanda 3-2 in Bamako and win a third match in Group K and move within one win of a place in the finals. Mamadou Camara snatched their late winner. African Footballer of the Year Achraf Hakimi scored twice as Morocco beat Niger 5-1 in Casablanca to maintain their perfect start in Group A and move closer to qualification. There are three more matches on Saturday to complete the third round of the group qualifiers which marks the halfway mark of the campaign.  The fourth round of group fixtures is on Monday and Tuesday and the last two rounds in March. The 2027 finals are to be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19-July 17.

Source: Reuters

PARIS, Nov 13 : France beat South Africa 21-19 in a tactically intriguing contest on Friday, with Fabien Galthie's side overcoming the world champions after outfoxing Rassie Erasmus in a battle of coaching gambles. South Africa's wholesale front-row changes had little impact on France's own ploy, with Antoine Dupont named at flyhalf before moving to his customary scrumhalf role during the match. Dupont played a key role as the Six Nations champions secured their first victory over South Africa at the Stade de France since 2005. Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey scored France's tries, while Maxime Lucu kicked six points. Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Cobus Reinach and Malcolm Marx crossed for South Africa, with Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu converting the first two tries. Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card after his yellow card was upgraded by the bunker review system for a dangerous clear-out at a ruck.

The victory left France on top of the Northern Hemisphere standings on 21 points. South Africa, suffering their first defeat of the Nations Championship, remained top of the Southern Hemisphere table on 21 points but could come under pressure from New Zealand. France’s win underlined their credentials as contenders for the 2027 World Cup, exactly a year before the final, after they had lost nine of their previous 10 meetings with the Springboks. That run included a one-point quarter-final defeat on home soil at the 2023 World Cup and a 32-17 loss last year, when South Africa had a player sent off before halftime. France’s preparations were again disrupted by injuries, with hooker Julien Marchand hurt in the warm-up and replaced by Peato Mauvaka. Flyhalf Romain Ntamack had dislocated his shoulder in last week’s win over Fiji and, with Matthieu Jalibert, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy also sidelined, Galthie handed Dupont his first international start at flyhalf and selected Lucu at scrumhalf. The shirt numbers proved deceptive, however, as Dupont operated predominantly in his customary scrumhalf role and Lucu filled in at flyhalf, as he had after replacing Ntamack against Fiji. UNCERTAINTY OVER ROLES "It's an idea I put to them when we knew Ntamack wouldn’t be playing," Galthie told a press conference. "They had a discussion, we watched a few matches, and we had a 40-minute training session and a 10-minute team run to set it up. I think it worked really well. Both of them played an outstanding game." South Africa had expected the pair to swap roles during the match, but Erasmus said the uncertainty made France harder to prepare for. "They have, at one position, a lot of injuries, but having Lucu and Dupont maybe strengthened the team in a way," Erasmus told reporters. "(Dupont) is a brilliant player and it's difficult to plan against, especially when we didn't know he was going to play 10 or 9." The pair were influential throughout as France made the most of Lood de Jager’s 13th-minute yellow card for a high tackle on Lucu, scoring twice during his absence. Dupont passed to Lucu in the move that ended with Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang scoring the opening try before the France captain’s left-footed 50-22 kick created the platform for Attissogbe’s effort. Dupont then sent Bielle-Biarrey over with a grubber kick in the 32nd minute. South Africa were forced to chase the game but Jan-Hendrik Wessels, drafted into the starting side when Erasmus reshuffled his front row about an hour before kick-off, scored from a lineout maul on the half-hour. Errors and indiscipline disrupted the second half, with Wiese handed a 20-minute red card before Grandidier-Nkanang was sent to the sin bin six minutes later for a deliberate knock-on. The winger’s yellow card came just as Lucu returned after being sin-binned for a high tackle shortly before halftime. Reinach powered over a minute later and South Africa dominated much of the second half before Marx scored from another maul after France tighthead prop Regis Montagne was shown a yellow card. Libbok had the chance to level the scores but sent the conversion wide with seven minutes remaining. France then survived a final South African attack before the home crowd erupted at the final whistle. The match marked the first time a sporting event had been staged at the Stade de France on November 13 since the 2015 Paris attacks, which began outside the stadium. France face Argentina next week, while South Africa travel to Ireland, before the teams could meet again in the final.

Nov 13 : Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match suspension by the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee following the challenge that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. Owono and De Miguel collided during a Spanish second-tier match between FC Andorra and Tenerife on November 2. De Miguel was taken to intensive care and died the following day. The committee said Owono had committed a serious infringement under Article 102 of the Royal Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary code, for violent conduct against an opponent during play that causes serious injury. It imposed the maximum sanction, along with the associated fines set out in Article 52 of the code.

"The referee's own description makes it possible to appreciate the particular seriousness of the action, both because of the way it was carried out, with the leg raised, and because of the forcefulness of the impact, which the referee expressly described as excessive," the committee said. "It is public knowledge that the tragic outcome of the events was the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," it added, saying that the particular seriousness of the case justified "the imposition of the sanction at its maximum level". Owono, 25, withdrew from Equatorial Guinea's squad for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month following De Miguel’s death. FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said on Thursday that Owono had yet to decide whether he would return to competition, adding the club would give the goalkeeper time and space to make that decision. Owono said last week that he was living through "the most difficult days of my life", while the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation said he was experiencing profound sorrow and grief.
